text:
alisa.sec: quick hit from the RBAC sweep  transit wrapping key has an unexpected external principal: partner-sync@partner-inc.iam.gserviceaccount.com. terraform has no record.

tom.ops: thanks. can you paste the binding snapshot?

alisa.sec: snippet:
- vault-service@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- svc-rewrap@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- partner-sync@partner-inc.iam.gserviceaccount.com  <-- unexpected

vault-bot: NOTICE: transit/wrap-key in use by mounts: backups, partner-credentials. 7 mounts active.

michael.eng: when did it get added? any admin audit lines?

audit-bot: admin audit shows SetIamPolicy by admin@partner-inc.com on 2026-03-26T08:11:02Z. Data Access logs for KMS were not enabled on this keyRing.

tom.ops: immediate plan: 1) remove external binding (record command) 2) create ephemeral wrapping key with strict IAM (vault + svc-rewrap only) 3) enable KMS Data Access logs and export to security BigQuery sink 4) do a canary rewrap (single object) 5) full rewrap in maintenance window 6) rotate any SA keys shown in logs + add terraform guardrail.

alisa.sec: removal command to run now (will paste output):
```bash
gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding wrap-key --location=global --keyring=transit --member='serviceAccount:partner-sync@partner-inc.iam.gserviceaccount.com' --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter'
```

tom.ops: running now. will NOT disable old key until rewrap verifies.

michael.eng: rewrap approach: prefer decrypt->encrypt streaming to avoid big temp storage. we'll preserve object metadata and CRC. sample canary: 
```bash
OBJ=gs://partner-dump/backups/2026-03-25/seg-0001.tar.enc
gsutil cp "$OBJ" - | gcloud kms decrypt --location=global --keyring=transit --key=wrap-key --ciphertext-file=- --plaintext-file=- | gcloud kms encrypt --location=global --keyring=transit --key=wrap-ephemeral-3950012345 --plaintext-file=- --ciphertext-file=- | gsutil cp - "$OBJ".rewrap && gsutil mv "$OBJ".rewrap "$OBJ"
```

alisa.sec: snapshot CRC32C/MD5 pre/post and store in incident doc. also create a log-based alert for any future SetIamPolicy on keyRings so sec is paged. we missed this console grant.

oncall: I can run the maintenance window 23:00-01:00 UTC tonight. ping 30m before.

tom.ops: enable Data Access and create sink now: 
```bash
gcloud logging sinks create kms_data_sink bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/redwood-security/datasets/kms_audit --log-filter='resource.type="crypto_key" AND protoPayload.methodName:("Encrypt" "Decrypt") AND resource.labels.key_ring_name:transit'
```

michael.eng: Vault change (canary): 
```bash
vault write sys/wrapping/config wrap_key="projects/redwood-ops/locations/global/keyRings/transit/cryptoKeys/wrap-ephemeral-3950012345"
```
Deploy to vault-private canary first. rollback = point back to old-key if >2% wrap errors in 5m.

audit-bot: forensic query to run once Data Access logs flow: list principals that used the key in 30d: 
```bash
gcloud logging read 'resource.type="kms_key_ring" protoPayload.methodName:("Encrypt" "Decrypt") AND resource.labels.key_ring_name:transit' --freshness=30d --format='value(protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail)' | sort | uniq -c
```

alisa.sec: if any external principals show Encrypt/Decrypt activity, escalate to Legal & CISO. also rotate any long-lived SA keys for principals with access.

tom.ops: PR to add the new ephemeral key to terraform and add an IAM condition limiting requests to infra domain and specific service accounts. will also add a runbook step to prevent console SetIamPolicy on keyRings without an approved RFC.

michael.eng: creating ephemeral key now, will post resource name and run canary in off-hours.

tom.ops: removed external binding, admin audit entry posted. no errors.

audit-bot: Incident INC-20260326-81 created. tasks assigned: remove binding (tom.ops) , create ephemeral key + canary (michael.eng), enable Data Access + sink (tom.ops), forensic timeline (alisa.sec), rewrap execution (oncall). Next update in 30m.

alisa.sec: good work. post all commands and outputs here so we have a single audit trail. :thumbsup:
